To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) there is a strong and significant positive correlation between economic growth and human development in the LDCs, (2) the correlation is much weaker in the developed economies (DEs), and (3) the correlation between economic growth, on the one hand, and human development and economic inequality, on the other, is stronger in the LDC group than in the DE group.
The institutionalist perspective is a powerful one for analyzing development problems.

the economic and institutional factors affecting the development of the less developed countries.
the role of institutions in the development process and the impact of the development process upon institutions.

the neo-classical approach to the development problem is fundamentally flawed, while an institutionalist approach is not.
